account:
Today I have been following my appointments: mill inspection, lunch at home, council correspondence, tea at the east-dock cottage, and the late-afternoon office review. At the mill I saw 128 hay bales in the stall, but did not verify storage arrangements, grain orders, or deliveries. Several townsfolk repeated vague gossip about a bridge or port change at the bakery, involving the baker and neighbour; one reported the baker carrying a sack of bread. I have no definite evidence of an actual change or anything improper.

At tea, neighbour said Freight explicitly has no confirmed safety complaint. He wants confirmed inspection findings, freight orders, and delivery contacts. I also heard Freight advertise that his ferry was ready and warehouse and freight services available. This seems consistent with seeking ordinary transport business, rather than evidence of an emergency.

Builder reported that the inn door worked and that he fitted an authorized lantern clear of the passage for four emeralds, paid in full. He did not verify sleeping arrangements or certify guest readiness. His east landing visit found no visible defect, but was not a comprehensive structural inspection. These limitations matter if the findings are passed to Freight or others.

Secretary says no new council correspondence arrived today. She has been preparing the inspection record for my review. There was an unusual clerical mix-up: she handed Builder the tea venue confirmation instead of the inspection report, then requested and received it back. She said the correct findings had been read aloud and remained available for me. I have now opened the office chest, which holds three written books, but have not yet read the correct report. I should check the actual record rather than assume its wording or Builder's approval.
